column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article gives conflicting dates for first Spanish settlement (1530, 1540, 1614); left out. Entry's Walker episode not in article.

Article's 'third largest city' and similar rankings, expatriate ratings and cost-of-living claims left out. Entry says cathedral begun c. 1125 and article says completed 1125: avoided saying begun; said founding year counted as 1125 when completed. Entry says 'bishop's seat'; article does not, not repeated.
Article: Stoicism founded c. 300 BCE; also says near the end of the fourth century BCE; dates avoided beyond that. Article says flourished until 3rd century CE; not stated.
Casualty figures conflict within the article (lead vs body); left out. Ceasefire dates for Syria conflict (10/11 June); left out; entry says 5-10 June.
Article says capital of Principality of Transylvania 1692-1791 and 1849-65 (lead) but 1699 in history; left out dates. Entry says Habsburg government seat in the 18th century; not repeated.

Entry says Napoleon attached it to his Kingdom of Italy in 1810 and it returned to Austria in 1815: not in the article, not repeated. Entry says 'now an autonomous province'; fine. Left out GDP rankings and 2026 population.
Left out characterisations of the regime and polls. ICJ finding left out.
Left out the cartel/violence paragraph, rankings, GDP, governor. Entry says Jesuits from the 1590s; article says 1599: consistent.

Article contradicts itself on where Isabella was proclaimed/crowned (church of San Miguel vs Plaza Mayor); place left out. Entry says aqueduct 'probably around end of 1st century CE'; article says late 1st or early 2nd century; consistent.
Entry's Chagatai/Mongol material is not in the article, left out. Article lead says origins stem from Mongolia and northern Europe/Siberia; omitted as asserted in thin section.

Entry says Ahmadnagar annexed 1636; article says Daulatabad captured and Husein Shah imprisoned 1632, Golconda 1635, Bijapur 1636. Left out year of Daulatabad. Entry says reign from 1628; article lead 1628 but crowned after Oct 1627: avoided a year. Famine toll attributed as reported.
Entry says pledged in 1469 (article: Orkney 1468, Shetland 1469; annexed 1472): consistent. Entry's Picts not in article. Left out rankings and current figures.

Entry says Russia on the France-Austria side; article treats Russia as briefly in Britain-Prussia coalition after Peter III (1762); I avoided assigning Russia to a side. Entry says Treaty of Paris transferred most French Indian holdings to Britain; article says Britain established commercial dominance in India: not asserted either way. Article says Spain's ally status 1762 'losing Havana and Manila'. Article says 'war ... 1756 to 1763'; Britain declared war 17 May 1756 'nearly two years after fighting' in Ohio: left out.
Left out population, politics and economic percentages.
Entry says c. 1831; article says 1831-37: birth year left out. Fight tallies in the article are inconsistent: left out.
Entry mentions a Soviet republic of 1918, not in the article. Population figures conflict in the article; left out.
Left out recent water-level and desalination developments. Entry says Saladin manoeuvred Crusaders into waterless terrain; article says cut off from lake; consistent.
Entry: Ottomans took it in 1479; article: sieges 1478-79, fell 1479. Consistent.
Entry's Arevaci and wool trade not in article (article says cattle industry). Article says Soria became part of Castile definitively in 1134 but also that Alfonso VII of León took control; left out.
Entry says Shah Mir and Chak sultans; article mentions Shah Mir only. Present-day politics omitted.

Article does not mention the 1696-97 Iberville raid in the entry; left out. Article gives Cabot's landing as 1494 (Sebastian Cabot) or 1497 (British and French historians), both attributed. Incorporation 1888 and 1892 fire from article. Population figures left out (as-of dates).
Article's approval ratings, public image, Pandora Papers and 2019 protests left out as recent or judgemental. Brief death fact included under In office.

Article gives birth c.1160, after c.1220 and Minister of Finance from 1191; the entry says only late 12th-early 13th century, so these were left out. Treasurer role kept as legend/document per the entry.

Article puts the first historical bishop, Theodore (d. 391), in the 4th century, with the see first at Octodurum; entry says bishop since late 6th century and 999 counts. Both left out; only 'oldest diocese in Switzerland' kept. Olympic bids and population figures left out.

Article: Ine pushed West Saxon boundaries west to include Somerset by early eighth century; entry says taken into Wessex in 7th century. Left undated in text. Athelney/Alfred 878 not in the article. Population figures left out.
Article's GDP comparison with Europe left out (ranking-type claim).
Article gives 1936 settlement; entry matches. Reputation paragraph and Donetsk airport left out (recent events).

Article's evaluative language (Gestapo comparison, 'economic mismanagement', 'autocracy') left out; Jatiya Rakkhi Bahini stated as accused. 2004 BBC poll left out. The article says he was 'president and prime minister from 1972'; entry says prime minister then president, so order kept as the entry.

Article: summer capital 1864 (lead) vs decision 1863; Simla Conference 1945 (article) vs 1914 (entry says Conference; article says Convention 1914): conference dates avoided. Himachal formation date (1948 vs 1971) left out.
Entry says its name is legally protected as a mark of origin; article does not say so and the text omits it. Recent events (2024 attack) left out; 1993 arson omitted as unneeded.
Article: orbit apogee 950 km vs intended 1,450 km; text says about 500 km lower. Article gives the launch as 4 October UTC (5 October local), entry says 4 October; both mentioned.
Entry says 'monitoring posts' south of frontier; article says Limes Tripolitanus. Not repeated.
Production figures, trade and biofuel details left out (dated). Entry's list of African empires not in article; not repeated.
Entry says created after 1871 abolition; article agrees roughly (1871-81). Liancourt Rocks dispute and population figures left out (current affairs, as-of).
Population figures and Lebanese ranking left out. Entry's 'purple dye and glass' matches article.
Entry says Nassau-Siegen residence from 1606; article gives neither 1606 nor 13th-century Nassau tenure; not repeated. Rubens' birth year not in article; omitted.
Left out: all events from 2015 on (UAE/STC), population figures, ecological threats.
Birth year c. 103 BC is one modern author's estimate; left as 'about 30'. Entry's 'thousands of rebels' matches 6,000.
Population, rankings and Smart Cities Mission left out (dated).
Population figures left out. 1993 Madımak hotel fire left out. Armenian population figures after 1914 left out.

Article gives Japan's surrender as 2 September 1945 and the Nanjing ceremony as 9 September; its Legacy section says the PRC observes 3 September as the day Japan surrendered in Tokyo. Left 3 September out. Article lead says civilians deaths 'around 20 million'; body says 10-20 million with consensus 15-16 million. Used the body's figures.

Article gives Selim as 'Selim the Grim'; not used. Article says Selim was 'one of the empire's most successful and respected rulers': left out as judgement. Entry says Safavids defeated at Chaldiran 1514; article text given only mentions 1514 in relation to the march; kept consistent.

Entry gives construction 1473-1481 and Last Judgement 1536-1541; article gives 1535-1541 in one place and 1537-1541 in another, so the Last Judgement is dated 'finishing in 1541' in text because article gives 1535, 1536/1537 inconsistently. Article: frescoes finished 1482; consecrated 1483.
Entry says the Berlin Conference gave it diplomatic form; article says 'regulated' and 'emblematic'.

Article contradicts itself on retirement: says she served until retirement in 2000, two months before her death, yet died 10 October 2000 voting in election. Left retirement out. Article calls her 'first woman in world democratically elected prime minister'; entry says first woman prime minister; used the latter wording. Left out the 1980 loss of civic rights and the contested assessments; left out Sirisena's views as present-day politics. 'funded parochial schools' means state-funded ones; word it carefully.
Entry gives 1898 only; article gives 21 April to 13 August. Article says Maine cause was a mysterious explosion; no blame stated.
Entry says treaties after WWI assigned region to Austria; article names the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (1919). Used. Left out dental tourism and the current EU trade claims.

Entry says renamed Justinianopolis under Byzantine rule; article does not mention it, left out. Article implies Ribat built after 870 (marble from Melite captured then) but Great Mosque section says mosque 850-851 was built almost thirty years after the Ribat. Contradiction; left both datings to 'Aghlabid period' / '9th century'. Left out the 2015 attack and recent population figures.

Entry says Cornovii heartland, 'later part of Powys and then Mercia'. Article only names Viroconium Cornoviorum and gives Powys after Rome then Mercia; no mention of Cornovii as a people, so kept to the city. Salop dates: article says Salop became official name after 1972 Local Government Act, renamed Shropshire 1 April 1980.
Left out recent politics (2008 war, EU status, blockade).

Article contradicts itself: palace built 1762, but city moved to present site after flood in 1772. Left flood date out. Entry says khanate from 1740s: article says 1743; fine. Article gives 1850-70 as the peak silk years; given as mid-19th century.

Entry says Pepin the Short proclaimed king at Soissons in 751; article does not say this, only that the Merovingian dynasty ran to 751 and the 744 council. Left the 751 proclamation out. Article says Syagrius ruled 457-486 as Kingdom of Soissons; entry says Clovis defeated Syagrius near the city in 486. Consistent.

Article claims Stafford became capital of Mercia in early tenth century; entry says Mercia's bishopric was at Lichfield. The Mercian capital claim is odd (Mercia ended as a kingdom in 918); I repeated it only as the article gives it - editor may want to remove. Left out the July 2026 reorganisation announcement and political, sport and company lists.
Article's first-shogun sources disagree; hedged. Article lead says Kamakura 1185 vs 1192 for the title; gave 1185 for ascendancy and 1192 for the title as the article does.

Entry says ruled by Siam from late 18th century until Franco-Siamese treaty of 1907; article says 1795 to 1907. Consistent. Article's tradition story is itself dubious (Ang Chan reign 1516-1566 vs Maha Chakkraphat 1548-1569); told only as oral tradition and noted as disputed.

Entry says Battle of Jutland 1916 fought off its entrance; article says fought 'here' 31 May-1 June 1916. Consistent enough; text uses article's wording. Article's Thyborøn channel description is garbled ('through Skagerrak'); wording rephrased cautiously as linking the North Sea to the Kattegat via the Limfjord.
Entry says 'for twenty-five years resisted'; no figure printed. Mother's origin disputed (Slavic princess or Muzaka family); left out of text.
Entry says her son was sold illegally to Alabama; not in the given excerpt, left out.
Entry says it fell to the Normans in the 12th century; article gives 1137, Roger II of Sicily. Consistent. Left out the Queen Giovanna legend as unsourced.

Entry says founded as New Archangel in 1804, capital of Russian America 1808, territorial capital until 1906; none of these is in the article, which gives 1799 settlement and Russian rule 1799-1867. Left 1804, 1808 and 1906 out; the 1799 fort is the article's start. Article's 'Crimean War' motive for the sale is the article's account; attributed with 'according to the account'. Entry says 1802 destruction; consistent.
Article gives arrest 18 August and death 12 September 1977; consistent with the entry.
Article dates the medina's building 849-851 and its walls' architecture to 1306; left out.

Entry mentions Tróia fish-salting complex; article does not, so only the Roman fish-salting factories are stated. Article's claim that the first treaty dividing the world was signed at the Convent of Jesus left out (doubtful).
Article's Historia Augusta anecdotes (temple to Jesus, oratory images) left out as unreliable. Article says the Persian war's outcome differs by source (Herodian vs Historia Augusta).
Article gives exact death date 23 September 1241 in lead but 'autumn of 1241' in body; text uses autumn.
Article dates Timur's birth 'between late 1320s and 1336'; entry says 1336; left out. Roxanna/Alexander in article is as stated. Article text on UNESCO danger listing since 2016 omitted.
Article's 'wat' is for Cambodia and nearby regions; stated as Cambodia. Pashupati seal omitted as speculative.

Entry names Babylonian, Chaldean, Hittite, Macedonian and Ottoman siegecraft; the article does not, so only the Assyrians and Alexander's Macedonians are covered. Entry's title is Siege warfare, article is Siege.
Entry says founded 1641 by settlers from Wethersfield; article says deed signed 1 July 1640. Both founding dates left out.
Article has 'Siemens AG ... Munich and Berlin' in lead and Munich in body; used Munich. Article gives bribery fine 'approximately $1.6 billion'. Spin-off of Healthineers 2017 as listed company.
Entry says Mohr came to Oberndorf in 1817; text omits this. Article's chart-position list omitted.
Entry says Bell Labs 1954 and satellites by 1960s; the article does not mention 1954, so not repeated. Article's 'first photovoltaic cell' is by Becquerel as entry states.
Entry describes Stirling Bridge 1297, Bannockburn 1314 and the Maeatae; the article does not, so left out. Article gives two city populations (38,587 and 49,928); omitted.
Pitcairn conversion in the entry is not in the article; not repeated. Membership figures and rankings omitted as time-bound.

Entry mentions Zanj rebels in the 9th century; the article does not. Article says Iran 'continues' to call it Arvand; omitted. The article is inconsistent: Zuhab 'temporarily lost'; used only 'permanently ceded'.

Entry says Carthago Nova captured 209 BCE and invasion of Africa 204 BCE with Masinissa; excerpt gives neither year nor Masinissa, so left out. Article gives death dates 187, c.185, 183 BCE; text says 'most modern sources prefer 183'.
Entry says border on Yalu and Tumen; article says only expanded to approximate current extent. Entry says reign from 1418; consistent. Article's Hall of Worthies re-established 1420.
Entry: founded 1718 as Russian fort, Alash Orda government 1917-1920; consistent. Article calls it 'Alash Autonomy'. Population figures conflict in the article (312,764 vs over 350,000); omitted.

Entry says expelled in 1492 and 1497; article gives 1496 for Manuel's edict and does not mention 1497 as expulsion; the Portuguese year is left out. Entry's Caribbean, Suriname, Curaçao details are not in the article.
SKIPPED: the article is about the present-day State Duma of the Russian Federation; its material on the imperial Duma is about 150 words and adds little to the entry
Article dates in BC converted to BCE.

Article gives Selim's deposition in 1806 in one place and 29 May 1807 in another; entry says 1807. I give only the 29 May 1807 date for Mustafa IV's accession and no year for the deposition itself otherwise. Article says Selim was stabbed by the Chief Black Eunuch; another version differs; left out the manner of death.
Hyksos king Apophis not mentioned to avoid confusion with the serpent Apep.
Entry says location unknown; article suggests candidate sites; wording hedged. Ebla claim not in article, left out.
Economic figures, rankings and election results left out per rules. Entry's 'between the world wars' industries not in article.

Article gives birth 12 November 1648, entry c. 1648; no birth date printed. Article says she lived 27 years in San Jerónimo (from 1669 would be 1696): internal inconsistency; kept 'last 27 years' as stated.
Article dates competition from 1955 announcements; entry dates 1957-1975. Kept 1955 as a fact in Background, not as the start of the contest.
Entry says Lombards took Spoleto c.570; article gives duchy seat in 576: no year printed. Festival of the Two Worlds, Guy of Spoleto not in article, left out.
Article gives Seleucia's foundation as c.305 or 307 BCE; omitted. Article says Antioch 300 BCE.
Present-day election results and office-holders left out. 1918 election not in article text given; omitted. Entry says founded 1905: consistent.
Pena Palace builder not in the article given; not mentioned.
Population genetics and contemporary grievance sections left out.
Economic, demographic indices and political figures left out. Article history thin on named dynasties; only listed.
Article gives death toll 2,000 to 70,000 in body; lead 5,000 to 30,000. Used the lead.
Article's text on religious freedom and Jews not in the given excerpt; not added.
Two sections only; recent events and contested heritage claims left out.
Entry says King of the Romans from 1411; article: elected 1410 and again 1411; both given. Hohenzollern/Wettin grants not in given article; omitted.
Article is titled Sogdia; written as a people where the article allows. An Lushan Rebellion not in the given excerpt.
Article gives Teishi's death as 1000 (chronology) and 1001 (text); no year given. Article names the same last reference 1017; entry has 1017 or 1025.
Wikipedia article is about the seismometer in general; written only on the seismoscope history it contains. Article dates the device 'AD 132' as the entry; says 'is said to have invented'.
Peace at Linköping: article gives 28 September, no year; left out year. Entry says deposed 1599, matches. Left out grim details of Linköping Bloodbath.

Article says Duchy of Słupsk residence 1368-1478; entry says 14th and 15th centuries and passed to Brandenburg-Prussia 1653 while article says peace treaty of 1648: year left as 1648 treaty (entry says 1653 - possible disagreement; entry's 1653 not printed, article's 1648 treaty printed; editor may check). Omitted 2014 mayor, missile defence.
Article spells 'Sunanate'; I kept it as given (probably Sunanate of Surakarta = Sunanate). Left out population figures, 2024 legislature composition.
Entry says Ottoman conquest; article lists Ottoman three times 1411-1463, no conquest date: left out. Left out 2013 census numbers and politics after 2007.
Dedeagac is Alexandroupoli per article. Entry says Bulgaria lost most of Macedonia: consistent.

Entry says colony 280s BCE; article 284 BCE: consistent. Entry says Senones settled after sack of Rome c. 390 BCE; article says first settled in the 4th century BCE; I did not print 390. Article has an unfilled date '[?]' for Piccolomini lordship; omitted.

Article says Aurangzeb 'now emperor' in 1660 and Shaista Khan attack in Jan 1660 (inconsistent); omitted. Article's death section is empty; no death story told. Entry's Surat raid 1664 not in article; omitted. Birth date disputed; no date printed.
Entry's 10th-century burh and Welsh Pengwern/1403 battle are not in the supplied article text; not repeated.

Article gives 157 million and 155 million for collections and 21 vs nineteen museums: contradicts itself, so no counts printed. Benin Bronzes from the entry are not in the article; not repeated. Left out budgets, 2025 controversies and board lists.
Left out CIA/NED funding figures, post-2017 politics, regional list. Article says 38 regions in 1980s and 37 now; not printed.

Article's populations contradict (288,461 in 2008 vs 1,866,845 in 2017 for the larger area): none printed. Fountain move dated 1898 and 1899 in the article: left as 'end of the 1890s'. Roman Era section empty in the supplied text. Article says destroyed during Arab invasion: not printed since later says 10th-century houses.
Article says founded around 3rd century and 'capital 300 AD'; entry says ancient capital: consistent. Left out 2009 attack, 2026 collapse and Dubai pavilion.
Silistra name given as Drastar and Dristra in article; used Drastar. Entry's siege 971 consistent with the Byzantines taking it 971.

Article's 1593 battle has no date within the year; Ottoman capture 24 Aug 1593 per article. Entry says 9th-century seat of dukes: article names Braslav c. 898. Left out 1991 war casualty figures, 1945 killings (figures disputed in article) and 2020 earthquake.
Left out the Pyramid Text's sexual wording. Entry says Twelfth and Thirteenth Dynasty kings, Sobekneferu: not in supplied article, not repeated.
Entry says passed to the British in 1818 and cotton boom late 19th c.; neither is in the article, so not repeated. Article's history paragraph on Padmashalis is loosely worded; kept to its gist.
Article says 'Corrective Move' 22 June 1969; name change 'a year after the reforms' (constitution 30 Nov 1970) - entry says from 1970: consistent. Qahtan section cut off in supplied text.

Entry says Palembang-based 7th to 13th century; article says disintegration may have followed 1025 and centre possibly Jambi; 13th century not printed. Date of Kedukan Bukit given 16 June 682 and 605 Saka (683) in article: wrote 682 or 683.
Article gives the Bombardment as 1864 only; entry's 1863-64 not contradicted, year 1864 printed. Left out populations and Abe.
Jain version differs (brother Bhamandal) and is not told. Entry says Janakpur claims birthplace: consistent.
Article's early Alpine Slavs section is from the lead and section openings; nothing contradicting the entry found. Skipped genetics and post-1991 politics.
Article gives 'until the early 1980s' for the Soviet period; entry says 1980s; left out end date. Omitted present-day countries still following it.
Article: Romans captured it 345, 314, 305 BCE; entry mentions Second Samnite War only; no conflict. Duchy 1443 per article.
Article gives birth as 1092 or 1096; entry c. 1092; left birth year out. Article says Stephen-Henry died at Ramlah in 1101 (not printed).

Entry says bequeathed to the Pope; article only says ownership passed to the Catholic Church after Umberto II's death in 1983; used the article's wording. Left out fringe theories and 'as of 2025' blood statement.
Entry's Olbia / Golden Horde / Lithuania points are not in the article; not repeated or contradicted. Article says Chychyklia 156, Kodyma 149 km.
Entry says promoted as Putonghua from 1956; article does not give that date, so left out. Article's Singapore/Malaysia/Myanmar notes mostly omitted.
Article gives Stanserhorn summit height 1,898 m in sights but 1,819 m highest point in Stans territory; height left out.
Article's 'Britain annexed the Transvaal in 1877' etc. consistent with entry. Native African deaths 20,000 as per article.
Entry says widespread in Egypt, Syria, parts of Iran and SE Asia: consistent. Followers figure (350 million) left out as a statistic of present.
Article says Ashur-nadin-shumi was 'captured and executed' (lead) and elsewhere 'disappeared, presumably executed'; I wrote the hedged version. Dates BC converted to BCE.
Entry says strong in Assam, Bengal, Odisha with medieval king patrons; article names these states among large communities but not the kings; not repeated. Left out demographic estimates.
Suda gives alternative birth dates (556/552 or 532/528); entry c. 556: used modern consensus 556-468. Alphabet-letter invention claim left out.
Article dates reign 240-270 (disputed) and death 'most likely May 270'; entry says 241-272. Left out reign and death years and the co-regency/coronation dates. Christian footstool story left out.

Article says Sigmaringen part of principality 1576-1850, and 'came 1535 to be owned by Hohenzollern'; entry says granted by Habsburgs in 1530s (not in article; not repeated). Left out the Nazi-era T4 detail.
Article's lead gives Sonni dynasty c. 1464-1493 and the text Ali 1464-1492; both omitted. Askia Ishaq II dates not given.
Entry says 1959 saophas gave up powers; article does not mention it; not repeated. Left out all post-2010 politics and conflict.
Article does not describe the disaster behind the impeachment; kept vague. Article body is silent on death year; entry 1095 used nowhere.
Article has nothing on history, the Nasrid emirate or irrigation; those entry claims are not repeated. Only two sections for lack of material.

Entry says it declined in favour of Uppsala and Stockholm and mentions a bishop's seat; article attributes decline to navigability from land rise; did not state the entry's cause. Coins: article 'end of 10th and beginning of 11th'; entry 'around 995'.

Article says the western extent of Slavonia as a region varies; text avoids giving boundaries beyond the counties. Population, GDP and agriculture shares left out as current figures. The 1868 settlement united the kingdoms; description agrees.

SKIPPED: Article has under about 250 words of substance beyond the description: it is a river course and hydrology list, with a pollution incident and recent floods that are excluded; no history of the river or its peoples.

Entry says he reversed earlier losses; article notes Armenia later partitioned 387 and Roman-Armenian gains in 371 largely neutralised 363 gains: text keeps both without stating Armenia was held at his death. Article lead says Armenia under Sasanian control at death; left out. Samudragupta/Kidara passage of the article is badly sourced and was not used.

Entry says the Somalis formed an important part of the Adal Sultanate; the saved article does not mention Adal, so the text does not either. The article gives several competing etymologies and a claim of 7000 years of indigeneity; left out the latter as unhedged.

Entry says the citadel was rebuilt in the 16th century; the article only says the town walls were built 1562-1594, so the citadel rebuilding is not stated. Entry calls the cathedral Romanesque, article gives 12th century only.

Entry names the Shebelle river and long-standing pastoral clans; the article names neither, so only pastoralism by implication (livestock figures). 2007 Abole oil field raid, current officials, courts, airports and the refugee camps left out as recent or administrative. Entry says Ogaden War was 1977-1978; article says 1977 only.

Entry says market rights about 1160 granted by Albert the Bear; the article says founded and granted Magdeburg rights about 1160, text follows the article. Entry calls the 1160 grant market rights; no conflict that matters. Article calls the Powder Tower about 1450 etc; not used.

Entry says Shamakhi was sacked in 1721; the article also quotes a source saying the sack was in 1717 (British Penny Cyclopaedia): text uses 1721 only. Article gives the Juma Mosque as built in the 8th century and later as a 10th-century mosque destroyed in 1902; text gives no building date. Entry says provincial capital moved to Baku after 1859; the article adds that it moved twice (also after 1191).

Entry says Sikhism was founded in the early 16th century and had nine succeeding Gurus; the article says late 15th century and refers to ten Gurus counting Nanak. Neither is printed. Article has nothing on the misls; the entry mentions them, the text does not. Khalistan movement and 2001 hate crimes left out as current affairs.

Entry gives only 26th century BCE; the article gives reign estimates c. 2613-2589 BCE (Oxford History) and others, so the text gives lengths only. Entry says the ships were probably from Byblos; the article says cedar most likely from Lebanon, and the Palermo Stone line says pine-wood; text says wood. Article mentions the Bent Pyramid reopened 2019: left out. Article and entry agree Palermo Stone records Nubia.

Entry says begun by Matthias of Arras and Peter Parler; consistent. Article gives Parler death as 1397 and also 1399: both dates left out. Ownership disputes (courts, 2006-2013) and the 2026 organ left out as recent events.

Entry says prince of Transylvania from 1571; the article says voivode 1571-1576 and prince from 1576: text says voivode. Article says Livonian War truce year Yam Zapolsky 15 January 1582; entry says 1582. Article names the Danzig sum as 200,000 zlotys in gold. "By 1573" for Bekes: the article also mentions a later Battle of Kerelőszentpál, left out.
SKIPPED: Article is about 400 words, mostly lists of notable people, firms and sport; the only history is the silver-mining boom, already in the description.

Entry dates the event c. 1177 BCE and says Hittite accounts identify them as immediate agents of the collapse; the article dates Ramesses III year 8 to 1175 BCE and says recent work views them as refugees. The text gives no year for year 8, and attributes the refugee view to recent work, so the text is softer than the entry on agency. Editor may wish to revise the entry. Group identifications are the article's hedged ones (Sicily, Teucri omitted).

Entry says d. 1995 and says he introduced a Latin script for Somali; the article says only a new writing system, so the text says nothing of the script. The article has long sections on CIA assessments, corruption and economy that read as advocacy; not used. Birth year given by article as c. 1919 in lead and 1909-1921 in text: text uses the range.

Entry says founded at the start of the nineteenth century; article says Lahore captured 1799, crowned 1801: text gives both. Article says the empire peaked in the mid-19th century and has population estimates from 5.35 to 15 million with conflicting religious shares: text says only that estimates vary and that most were Muslim (both of the article's breakdowns give a Muslim majority or plurality, one 80 percent, one 51 percent: so "most" is loose; editor may change to "many").

Entry says conquered Serbia in 924 but defeated by the Croats; article gives the Croatian defeat of his troops in 926 (under Alogobotur), included. Article says Cyrillic developed at Preslav in the 890s and at Ohrid; text says the schools. Heading "Death and legacy" used for culture; death told in Reign.

Entry says founded by Dharmapala in the late eighth century; the article says seals identify Dharmapala but Tibetan sources credit his successor Devapala (c. 810-850) after the conquest of Varendra: the text gives only the seal evidence. The article says the nearby Halud and Sitakot viharas date from the same period; left out as unclear.

Entry says the Legion moved to Aubagne in 1962; the article does not say so, so left out. Article says the city was associated with the Legion from the 1830s while giving the camp as 1843: text says only until 1962. Tramway of 2017 and the notes on neighbourhoods left out.
Entry says the river flows west through Picardy past Saint-Quentin, Amiens and Abbeville; article agrees. Floods of 2001 left out.

Entry says duchies received in 1737; article says abdication 26 January 1736 with the duchies as compensation and the Peace of Vienna 1738. Year of receipt left out; the 1736 abdication kept as the article's date. Article says 'Maria', entry says Marie.

Article gives 330 tons of gas in the lead and 300-500 tons in the war crimes section; only 330 tons printed. Article says 'Ethiopian guerilla resistance until 1941'; Italian guerrilla until 1943 not used.
Entry: Ottomans captured 1383 (matches article's definitive date; article also has a brief capture in 1371, left out). Entry says Dušan took it in 1345 from Byzantium; consistent.

Article says Mansurah 'ended 11 February 1250'; prose follows it. Entry says Louis 'captured during the retreat'; article has the capture after Mansurah and the retreat to Fariskur; wording kept vague. Article says Jerusalem lost 1244 (loss of the Holy City); I wrote 'had already been lost'.

Article: 'Marco Polo visited the city' stated flatly; I wrote 'is said to have' - actually article has no hedge; may remove hedge. Left as is for safety. Entry says Bactrian Gold found 1978 (article too); article elsewhere says excavation 1969-1979 and 1977; avoided stating a discovery year. Left out the Dasht-i-Leili massacre of 2001 and the 2021 capture: recent events/not needed.
Article says desc: leaders Pechersky and Feldhendler - article text provided names Pechersky; Feldhendler is in the entry's desc, not seen in the shown article portion. Check flag.

Article is mostly lists; the entry's claims on residence from 1599 and the court orchestra are not in the article and were not used. Short text (about 260 words). The article's 'Jewish bath' and 'mikveh' are listed separately; only one mention used.
